stories.headline: Odisha CM Mohan Majhi cancels Diwali celebrations over Cyclone Arnab damage
stories.title: Odisha CM Mohan Majhi cancels Diwali celebrations over Cyclone Arnab damage
stories.summary: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has cancelled Diwali celebrations at his residence this year in view of the damage and suffering caused by Cyclone Arnab and subsequent floods in several parts of the state. In a statement, the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) said Diwali celebrations at Majhi's residence have been cancelled. The CM has also requested people not to bring gifts or bouquets on the occasion. "The Hon'ble Chief Minister has appealed to people to remain sensitive to the public in the affected areas and extend a helping hand to those affected by the disaster," the CMO said in a post on X. Earlier, Majhi had also skipped Durga Puja celebrations as a mark of solidarity with farmers who suffered crop losses due to heavy rainfall in October. He had refrained from visiting puja pandals. The state's southern districts have been severely impacted following heavy rainfall and floods triggered by Cyclone Arnab, displacing thousands and causing extensive damage to property an

stories.headline: Former Odisha CM Naveen Patnaik visits Ganjam amidst criticism of not meeting flood-hit people
stories.title: Former Odisha CM Naveen Patnaik visits Ganjam amidst criticism of not meeting flood-hit people
stories.summary: Recently, posters portraying Mr. Patnaik as missing appeared in Hinjili, his home constituency, triggering a war of words between the ruling BJP and the Opposition BJD
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha Leader of Opposition and former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik on Saturday (November 7, 2026) visited Ganjam, his home district, which was badly affected by floods caused by Cyclone Arnab, after the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party accused him of being indifferent to his own constituency.
His visit came 10 days after extremely heavy rain poured in Ganjam rendering thousands of families homeless, destroying acres of ready to harvest paddy crops and damaging livelihood of people.
Mr. Patnaik toured Sheragada, an area devastated by floods, in Hinjili Assembly constituency, from where he has been continuously elected since 2000.
Besides, the Leader of Opposition met people in Asika and Sorada areas where he expressed solidarity with flood affected people, said a senior Biju Janata Dal leader.
“Thousands of people gathered at different locations to meet Mr. Patnaik and share their plight with their leader.

Farmers, carrying damaged paddy stalks and sugarcane plants, expressed anguish over their losses, alleging that government apathy in managing the floods had ruined their livelihoods,” the BJD said in a statement.
The Leader of Opposition demanded that the government should expedite providing assistance to all affected families.

Even as the floods triggered by Cyclone Arnab emerged as one of the worst natural disasters to hit Ganjam, political sparring between the BJP and Opposition parties, particularly the BJD, intensified during the rescue and relief operations.
“The BJP government in Odisha failed to make a proper disaster plan ahead of Cyclone Arnab that made landfall in Andhra Pradesh.

There was warning of heavy rain over southern Odisha districts, yet the administration moved in a lackadaisical manner exposing people to the fury of nature,” said former IAS officer Sujata Rout, who recently joined the party.
As the BJD stepped up its attack over alleged public discontent with relief and rehabilitation efforts, posters portraying Mr. Patnaik as “missing” appeared in Hinjili.
The BJP had accused the former Chief Minister of criticising the government while abandoning his own constituency in its hour of crisis.

stories.title: Campus Election Row: Kerala High Court Asks Sree Sankaracharya University To Produce Observer's Email Cited To Postpone Polls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Kerala High Court on Thursday (06 November) directed the Sree Sankaracharya University to produce the email of the impartial observer that has been relied on by the varsity's Registrar to postpone the 2026-27 Campus Union and University Council elections.
Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan issued the direction in a plea moved by a student of the University challenging the university's decision...

Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan issued the direction in a plea moved by a student of the University challenging the university's decision to indefinitely postpone the 2026–27 Campus Union and University Union Council elections.
The election was originally scheduled to be held on October 16, but an order dated October 9 was issued by the University postponing the election.
The petitioner had submitted his nomination for the post of General Secretary of the Campus Union, and his candidature was accepted following scrutiny.

The petition alleges that several nominations submitted by students associated with the Akhila Bharatha Vidhyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the Kerala Students Union (KSU) were rejected by the Returning Officer on account of substantial defects.
Following the rejection, representatives of the two student organisations allegedly approached the Vice Chancellor with complaints.
It is further alleged that the Vice Chancellor subsequently directed the indefinite postponement of the elections, primarily on the basis of complaints raised by the student organisations.
The University, in its October 9 order cited reports of the Impartial Observer, which has alleged violations of the elections code of conduct and complaints received from various organisations.
It stated that outsiders had entered the campus after the enforcement of the code of conduct and that flags and banners of student organisations continued to be displayed on campus.

The order also referred to the failure to reach a consensus during discussions with representatives of different student organisations and stated that the elections were being postponed to ensure a peaceful, fair and orderly electoral process.

stories.headline: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Rajesh Bindal appointed NCLAT chairperson, ending interim arrangement
stories.title: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Rajesh Bindal appointed NCLAT chairperson, ending interim arrangement
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 07: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Rajesh Bindal has been appointed chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), filling the key position that had been held on an officiating basis since July 2026, according to a report by Livelaw. Justice Bindal, who served as a judge of the Supreme Court from February 13, 2023, to April 15, 2026, succeeds the interim arrangement under which Justice Yogesh Khanna had been discharging the duties of NCLAT chairperson following the completion of Justice Ashok Bhushan's tenure. Justice Bindal brings with him extensive judicial experience across several High Courts. He was elevated to the Punjab and Haryana High Court in 2006 before being transferred to the Jammu and Kashmir High Court in 2018. During his tenure in Jammu and Kashmir, he also served as the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court in December 2020. Subsequently, he was transferred to the Calcutta High Court in January 2021 and assumed charge as its Acting Chief Justice in April 2021. He took the oath as Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court on October 11, 2021, before his elevation to the Supreme Court in 2023. After retiring from the Supreme Court, he was appointed as Emeritus Professor at the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) and joined Galgotias University School of Law as an Honorary Distinguished Jurist. His appointment marks the end of the interim arrangement at the appellate tribunal, which deals with appeals arising from orders passed by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).

stories.headline: Supreme Court Disposes Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
stories.title: Supreme Court Disposes Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6) dismissed a plea challenging senior advocate designations conferred by the Allahabad High Court in 2019.
A bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe observed that the applicants who were not conferred the designation could apply afresh in the next round.
Advocate Pranav Sachdeva for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner was not considered despite having 15 years of unblemished continuous practice in Allahabad High Court.
However, Justice Narashimha questioned why he wanted to litigate the issue, responding, "Apply.
Why do you want to litigate?
You apply afresh.
Don't unnecessarily litigate."
Sachdeva alleged that the selection committee has not done the evaluation for several years despite the judgment in Jitendra Kalla.
State of NCT holding that at least one exercise of senior designation must be done every calendar year.
Ultimately, the Court ordered, "We are not inclined to interfere with the order passed by the High Court.

We make it clear that the petitioner will be entitled to reapply and upon such application it shall be considered in accordance with the law that governs the subject, including the principle laid down in Jitendra Kalla's case."
The Special Leave Petition was filed against the September 2024 judgment of the Allahabad High Court which rejected the petition filed by Advocate Vishnu Bihari Tiwari against the 2019 designations.
